changed.analysis:
The research established a bounded source-level diagnosis and a plausible first implementation boundary: restore directed tour-prerequisite storage and its reader on the recorded prod-derived baseline. It did not implement or demonstrate the automatic discount. This substantially supports the selected job’s decision-enabling purpose, but historical reuse readiness and executable compatibility remain unverified within this packet. The selected job explicitly required a version-bound connection assessment and left implementation and delivery validation to later work (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/distillation-routine-checks-v1/run/handoff.json, chosen_atom, “Done when” passage).

The version boundary is supported, with an important distinction. Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/observations.json, entries 0–2, records auto-50-perc-off and prod both resolving to 45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568, while the checked-out branch remained feature/kiosk-square-return-recovery. The status output lists untracked paths and no tracked changes. Thus this was inspection of the selected committed tree, not execution from a checked-out auto-50-perc-off worktree. The result’s inspected_committed_tree=true accurately preserves that distinction (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, baseline).

The first missing connection is reasonably supported within the inspected scope. The commit-tree listing contains neither the historical prerequisite migration/reader nor the named purchase-evidence services; the recorded prerequisite/automatic-discount identifier search returned no matches (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/observations.json, entries 3–4). The supplied Tours model has no prerequisite relationship, and UserDifferentTour only declares its table, key and timestamp setting (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Tours.php, class body; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/UserDifferentTour.php, class body). These support absence of the historical implementation and no identified equivalent in the traced source. They do not establish the contents of a live database, every differently named implementation, or why historical files are absent; a minimal Eloquent model does not enumerate its database schema.

Existing recognition and purchase surfaces are present, but their composition into qualifying evidence is missing from the traced checkout. HomeController::submitImage stores user, tour and selfie history with timeslot fields explicitly null; history-recording exceptions are caught without stopping the main flow. Its version-2 branch assigns matched product-image IDs to detectedFaceIds, and submitImageStream explicitly stores “matched image IDs in v2.” Therefore the research’s phrase “records ... face IDs” needs qualification: the stored identifiers are not uniformly Rekognition face IDs (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Http/Controllers/CustomerUser/HomeController.php, submitImage historical-tracking block and submitImageStream history block). AmazonFaceRecognitionService::searchFacesByImage returns similarity and a nullable externalImageId, plus distinct failure outcomes; this is a usable source interface, not evidence that a historical search can actually be resolved to the same person’s paid prerequisite purchase (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Helpers/AmazonFaceRecognitionService.php, searchFacesByImage).

Absence of the historical services must not be interpreted as absence of all purchase handling. HomeController::faceRecognitionProcess already joins recognized image associations to orders and payments with status_id=4, scoped to the authenticated user and requested timeslot. getPurchaseHistory also includes 100%-discount orders without a payment. Those are existing behaviors worth preserving, but neither establishes the required cross-tour qualification; a displayed purchase history entry is not necessarily a paid purchase (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Http/Controllers/CustomerUser/HomeController.php, faceRecognitionProcess queries q1/q2 and getPurchaseHistory).

The discount-path findings are supported by supplied source. ProductDiscount has fields, relationships and a unique-batch scope, but no automatic 50% selector (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/ProductDiscount.php, complete class). The customer routes connect order creation, checkout display, discount preview and payment (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/routes/web.php, customer checkout/payment routes). postCheckout reads a supplied redeem-code cookie; the view automatically previews an existing cookie code and submits the discount field for payment. This existing cookie automation is not automatic discovery based on prerequisite eligibility (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/resources/views/customer/checkout-refactored.blade.php, DataController.applyDiscount, document-ready initialization and ResponseController.buildPaymentData). CheckoutController::discount calculates a preview, while postPayment saves the discounted total and discount association before provider handling. Consequently, preview must be distinguished from persisted order discount application; neither path supplies the missing qualification and discovery mechanism (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Http/Controllers/CustomerUser/Checkout/CheckoutController.php, postCheckout, discount and postPayment).

The proposed restoration boundary is concrete: checkout-tour ID plus directed configured pairs produce configuration status and prerequisite IDs. It names configured/unconfigured tours, multiple prerequisites, direction and isolated rollback as acceptance cases, and protects existing tour rows and checkout/pricing/recognition/payment behavior. However, these are proposed acceptance cases, not fresh passing tests. The historical implementation, test and proof files appear only as references in this packet; their bodies and detailed hash-verification output are absent. The reported “15 of 15 verified” therefore cannot independently establish historical test coverage or compatibility here (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, first_supported_implementation_boundary and validation).

The demonstrated contribution is reduced uncertainty about this committed customer web path: restoration of a specific upstream dependency is justified more strongly than immediate integration of supposedly available historical components. It is not proof that restoration alone completes qualification or is the only possible implementation order. The research records zero fresh product tests, no live database/AWS/browser/payment/deployment testing, and incomplete tracing of the alternate kiosk API. Current-dependency tests and target MySQL compatibility remain outstanding. These limits prevent a claim of fully validated research coverage, implemented product progress, or delivery of the complete automatic-discount sequence (Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, validation, limits and first_supported_implementation_boundary.remaining_validation).

remaining.analysis:
Selected research job

The central research question is substantially answered: the inspected committed tree lacks the directed prerequisite structure, and the assessment identifies restoration of its storage and reader as the first implementation boundary. Inputs, outputs, historical artifact references, five acceptance cases and protected behavior are recorded. Implementation itself is explicitly later work, so its absence is not a research failure. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/distillation-routine-checks-v1/run/handoff.json, /chosen_atom, “Done when”; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /findings/0 and /first_supported_implementation_boundary.]

Three limitations remain in the research handoff:

1. Executable reuse and dependency compatibility remain unverified. The result reports “15 of 15” historical proof hashes verified but zero fresh product tests, and explicitly defers rerunning preserved tests against current dependencies. The packet contains historical artifact references, not their source/test bodies or detailed verification outputs. This supports a restoration candidate, not a demonstrated compatible restoration. The selected job requested focused existing tests where available; the packet does not explain whether those tests were runnable during this assessment or why none ran. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /validation and /first_supported_implementation_boundary/remaining_validation; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/distillation-routine-checks-v1/run/handoff.json, /selection_reasoning, “Where available, use existing focused tests”.]

2. Coverage beyond customer web checkout remains unresolved. The result explicitly says the alternate kiosk API path was not exhaustively traced. No supplied evidence establishes whether that separate path belongs to the intended delivery surface. This limits whole-product conclusions, although it does not erase the identified prerequisite gap in the inspected tree. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /limits/0–2.]

3. The historical recognition approach has not been reconciled fully with the baseline’s existing recognition variants. In HomeController, submitImage can store multiple-face selfie metadata, while submitImageStream stores matched image IDs as face IDs. The assessment identifies missing historical evidence services but does not establish compatibility across these representations or their linkage to a paid historical purchase. This is an unresolved downstream integration question, not evidence that the existing recognition flow is broken. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Http/Controllers/CustomerUser/HomeController.php, submitImage multi-face handling and submitImageStream, “Store face IDs (matched image IDs in v2)”; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /findings/2.]

Baseline identity is no longer missing. Both auto-50-perc-off and prod resolve to 45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568. However, the active worktree remained feature/kiosk-square-return-recovery with listed untracked files; the assessment inspected the target committed tree without switching checkout. It should not be described as testing a checked-out delivery branch. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/observations.json, entries 0–3; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /baseline.]

Fixed delivery goal

The product still needs the configured current-tour-to-prerequisite relationship and an integrated qualification path establishing the same person’s paid purchase at any one configured prerequisite tour. Existing selfie capture and recognition helpers are reusable surfaces, but the historical evidence services are absent from the inspected baseline, and restoring files alone would not establish that qualification. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/goal-record-v1/goal-context.json, /goal/outcome and /goal/completion_conditions/3–5; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /findings/0–2.]

Automatic discovery of an applicable existing 50% code and its connection to checkout before payment are also missing from the traced path. Supplied-code handling already exists: postCheckout reads a redeem-code cookie; the checkout view previews an entered or saved code; postPayment calculates and saves the discount before provider handling. That behavior does not implement purchase-based qualification or automatic code discovery. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/app/Http/Controllers/CustomerUser/Checkout/CheckoutController.php, postCheckout, discount and postPayment; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/source/resources/views/customer/checkout-refactored.blade.php, DataController.applyDiscount and document-ready redemption-code handling.]

Finally, delivery lacks version-bound execution evidence of the complete qualified checkout sequence and preservation of surrounding behavior. No fresh product, browser, live recognition, database, payment or deployment validation was performed. Actual prerequisite configuration, applicable code availability, target MySQL compatibility and deployed behavior therefore remain unknown—not demonstrated failures. These are delivery implementation/validation gaps, not requirements to turn this research job into a deployment exercise. [Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/loop-controller-prototype/baseline-capability-assessment-v1/result.json, /validation, /limits, /findings/3/limits and /first_supported_implementation_boundary/remaining_validation; Tasks/atom-selection-machinery-20260918/goal-record-v1/goal-context.json, /goal/outcome.]

achieved.statement: The research reduced uncertainty about the selected delivery baseline by assessing the committed tree at 45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568. The recorded worktree remained on feature/kiosk-square-return-recovery with untracked files; this was not execution from a checked-out delivery branch or evidence of today's checkout.

Within the inspected customer web path, the research identified the missing directed prerequisite relationship and absent historical purchase-evidence services. It documented a concrete restoration boundary with checkout-tour and configured-pair inputs, prerequisite-ID outputs, historical references, five acceptance cases and protected behavior. This is decision-enabling research, not an implemented restoration.

The source trace identifies reusable recognition and supplied-code handling. Checkout reads a redeem-code cookie, previews an entered or saved code, and saves the discounted order during postPayment before provider handling. That existing automation does not establish prerequisite-based qualification or automatic discovery of a 50% code.

remaining.statement: Overall delivery still requires the configured prerequisite relationship, same-person paid-purchase qualification through the existing recognition flow, applicable existing 50% code discovery, and automatic application before payment. The inspected source does not establish those integrated connections.

Recognition compatibility and purchase provenance remain unresolved. Stored identifiers differ by recognition variant: version 2 stores matched image IDs, historical tracking leaves timeslot fields null, and searchFacesByImage can return a null external reference. Existing purchase-history behavior also includes fully discounted orders without payment, so history presence alone cannot establish a qualifying paid purchase.

Executable reuse is unverified. The result reports 15 of 15 historical proof hashes verified, but the referenced historical source/test bodies and detailed verification outputs are not included here. Zero fresh product tests ran; compatibility with current dependencies and target MySQL remains outstanding. The packet does not explain whether focused existing tests were runnable or why none ran.

Version-bound execution evidence for the whole checkout sequence and preservation of surrounding behavior is missing. No live database, AWS, browser, payment or deployment behavior was tested; applicable code configuration was not queried. The alternate kiosk API was not exhaustively traced, and its inclusion in the intended delivery surface is not established by this packet.

E0146.text:
Already demonstrated: the supplied historical records support several bounded product atoms, only within their recorded boundaries. A directed tour-prerequisite structure passed five frozen isolated-SQLite cases. Prior-tour purchase eligibility passed seven installed cases with 324 assertions against controlled owner-derived SQLite fixtures. Search-payment evidence is historically reported as a controlled internal-service proof, not production payment verification, live discount eligibility, or checkout behavior. A usable 50% selector was historically reviewed as supported for deterministic selection or none, preservation of attributes and existing members, payment-usage guard execution, unchanged state, and promoted-path repetition; that still does not establish checkout installation or end-to-end checkout application.

The selfie-purchase-lookup atom demonstrated a bounded internal-service advance. Before that atom, RecognitionPurchaseEvidence exposed forMatches and forReference, but no forSelfie entrypoint; baseline executions reported available=false and no recognition request. After the atom, RecognitionPurchaseEvidence::forSelfie was added to query the fixed purchase-search-history collection through the configured Amazon face-recognition helper and return the existing full purchase-evidence resolver output through forMatches. Nine controlled actual-source executions validated empty matches, one paid match, unpaid-before-paid ordering, duplicate-reference preservation, provider failure/no-face/no-collection, invalid later reference, and missing-history behavior. The proof boundary is controlled SQLite fixtures and intercepted provider HTTP with a direct service call. This is bounded historical internal-service product progress, not checkout delivery, live same-person identity, prerequisite qualification, discount application, production deployment, or an autonomy gain.

For machinery/provenance, the input interview machinery is demonstrated for this intake purpose by a live chronological replay and by an installed-entry-point proof. The build-only atom builder is demonstrated as a build capability by captured-assignment validation and installed-controller validation; it accepts approved bounded atoms without comparative selection and does not generate or rank successor atoms. Under the fixed goal record, the delivery goal here is the Taggable automatic-discount product outcome; the historical machinery-development goal remains separate provenance rather than an additional completion condition for this product assessment.

The new delivery branch needs version-bound evidence that the relevant product pieces are present and wired through the real flow: prerequisite structure, eligibility service, payment and recognition evidence services, selector integration, automatic discount application in checkout before payment, preservation of surrounding checkout/search/payment behavior, tests through the real checkout path, and promotion or deployment evidence as applicable.

Still uncertain: whether the historical product files exist on the new `auto-50-perc-off` baseline branch, whether equivalent implementation exists under other names, what the exact current checkout code on that branch contains beyond the established baseline commit, whether live MySQL migration, production data, payment records, recognition behavior, and configured discount codes satisfy the intended flow, and whether the automatic 50% code has ever been applied in a real checkout. The earlier uncertainty about which branch is intended for delivery is resolved by the owner decision, but product completion remains unproved.

E0933.text:
Job: Establish the automatic-discount capability and first missing connection in taggable-server on auto-50-perc-off, based on prod commit 45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568. Produce one version-bound assessment tracing eligible current-tour checkout through prerequisite lookup, existing face-recognition qualification of the same person’s paid purchase at any one prerequisite tour, applicable existing 50% code selection, and application before payment. Keep routine access checks, source inspection, historical-artifact lookup and focused existing tests inside this job.

Why it matters: Historical component proofs make reuse plausible, but the selected baseline’s contents and checkout connections remain uninspected. Absence findings from another branch cannot justify restoration here. This assessment determines whether delivery needs reuse, integration or restoration of a specific dependency, enabling a bounded product change. No supplied evidence establishes an access blocker requiring a separate prerequisite job.

Done when: One concise evidence package records the inspected commit and worktree state, relevant checkout call path, and each required connection as supported, demonstrably missing, incompatible or unresolved. It cites source locations and historical provenance, distinguishes source inference from executed tests, and identifies the first supported implementation boundary with inputs, dependencies, acceptance cases and surrounding behavior to preserve. If the mechanism already exists, identify its remaining validation gap. If unavailable evidence prevents the determination, identify the exact blocker and bounded follow-up. Implementation and subsequent delivery validation remain later work; this assessment itself does not deliver the discount.

Full delivery still requires version-bound evidence of the qualified checkout sequence, automatic application before payment, and preservation of surrounding behavior.
